subject: Mutual Action Plan: long-window performance benchmark & close timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: long-window performance benchmark & close timeline

Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I put together a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) focused on performance verification for long-context usage and a proposed close timeline so we can coordinate procurement and deployment. High level goals: confirm throughput/latency and TTFT targets across realistic prompt-size distributions, validate KV-cache behavior for conversational workloads, and exercise concurrency up to expected production levels.

Scope and acceptance criteria (short):
- Workload: mix of short prompts (~64 tokens), medium (~2k tokens), long (~32k tokens), and tail long (>64k up to 256k) with distribution derived from your sample set.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end TTFT (time-to-first-token), tokens/sec throughput, CPU/GPU memory utilization, and KV cache hit/miss delta.
- Targets to pass: p95 TTFT <= 450 ms for medium prompts (2k) at concurrency 8; sustained throughput >= 22k tokens/sec for batch runs on dedicated instance class; graceful degradation policy verified when concurrency increases 2x above target.

Planned tests (detailed):
1) Warm/cold KV cache sweep: repeat a fixed conversational prefix set to measure warm cache improvement. Scenarios: cold-start, warm after single-session, warm after 100 sessions.
2) Sequence length scaling: single-request and batched runs at sequence lengths: 8k, 32k, 64k, 128k, 256k. Measure memory, latency, and tail behavior.
3) Prompt distribution run: 10k requests sampled from your anonymized distribution to get realistic P50/P95/P99 numbers and tokens/sec.
4) Concurrency stress: increase concurrent client threads (1, 8, 16, 32, 64) and verify autoscaling/fallback behavior.

Deliverables and timeline (proposed MAP):
- Aug 10: Provide sanitized prompt distribution + S3 access (ACME to provide) — owner: ACME (Tom)
- Aug 11-12: Redwood runs baseline tests (sequence scaling + KV sweep) — owner: Redwood SE (Dev)
- Aug 13: Results packet + slide deck with pass/fail and suggested config (attachments) — owner: Redwood (Karthik/Dev)
- Aug 14: Joint review call to finalize performance acceptance and finalize procurement timeline — owner: joint
- Aug 21: Procurement complete, Dedicated pool reserved, target deployment week of Aug 24 — ACME ops/procurement

Attachments I'll share after the runs: CSV with raw per-request latencies, slide deck with annotated charts, and an updated MAP PDF.

Questions/asks for you now: please confirm who will provide the sample prompt set (S3 link) and the target concurrency we should validate for initial rollout.

Thanks,

Sara/Karthik —

We completed the runs this morning and attached the raw CSV + slides. Summary of key findings below (high level):

1) Sequence length scaling (single-request median numbers):
- 8k tokens: p50 latency 120ms, p95 260ms, TTFT 80ms, tokens/sec 34k (GPU p100-equivalent cluster)
- 32k tokens: p50 latency 560ms, p95 1.3s, TTFT 420ms, tokens/sec 29k
- 64k tokens: p50 latency 1.1s, p95 2.4s, TTFT 850ms, tokens/sec 24k
- 128k tokens: p50 latency 2.6s, p95 4.9s, TTFT 1.9s, tokens/sec 18k
- 256k tokens: memory pressure caused occasional model swaps; p50 latency 5.8s, p95 12.1s, TTFT 4.5s, tokens/sec 9k

Observations: throughput decreases roughly linearly with sequence length due to self-attention and KV management. 128k and 256k require larger instance classes or aggressive quantization; we observed outlier p99s correlated with memory swapping.

2) KV cache warm vs cold (32k scenario, concurrency=8):
- Cold cache p95 TTFT: 670ms
- Warm cache p95 TTFT: 320ms (approx 52% improvement)
- After repeated session prefixes (100 sessions) p95 TTFT stabilized at ~300ms

3) Concurrency stress (32k workload mix):
- concurrency 1: p95 TTFT 410ms
- concurrency 8: p95 TTFT 620ms
- concurrency 16: p95 TTFT 1.1s (autoscaler triggered and added nodes)
- concurrency 32: p95 TTFT 2.5s with fallback to lower-cost model variant for 20% of requests (policy applied)

4) Resource lines: GPU memory utilization is the dominant constraint for >64k sequences; CPU transient load grows during KV serialization.

Recommended config for ACME initial rollout (concurrency target 16):
- Dedicated instance class: 8xA100-80GB equiv or 4xH100-80GB equiv with 1.5x warm cache capacity (reserve cache-hosting nodes).
- Enable prefix KV cache and set TTL to 30 minutes for session-aligned workloads.
- For sequences >128k, use streaming+chunking with a 2-token overlap and token-level reassembly to avoid swaps.
- Quantization to int8 gave ~1.3x throughput improvement but increased p95 jitter for 256k tests; recommend int8 for 8k-64k, keep fp16 for >128k runs.

I've attached the CSV (acme_longwindow_benchmark_results.csv) with per-request rows and the slides (long-context-test-slides.pdf) showing latency curves, memory maps, and a MAP update draft.

Action items we propose:
- Aug 13 11:00am PT: joint review (Karthik/Dev/Sara/Tom) to go through slides and finalize pass/fail.
- If pass, Redwood will send a dedicated capacity reservation estimate and draft contract addendum by Aug 14.

Thanks — happy to go deeper in any chart on the call.

Sara/Tom —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the detailed runs, Dev — this is exactly what we needed. Quick summary and next steps to lock the MAP and the close timeline:

Summary of pass criteria vs results:
- Medium prompts (2k): p95 TTFT target 450ms -> measured 420ms (PASS)
- Concurrency 16 baseline: p95 TTFT target 1.0s -> measured 1.1s with autoscale (marginal, OK if we reserve capacity)
- KV cache: expected warm improvement observed ~50% (PASS if we deploy cache-reserve nodes)
- Longest sequences (>128k): not production-passable without streaming; recommend streaming for initial rollout (RECOMMENDATION)

Updated MAP & close timeline:
- Aug 13 11:00am PT: joint technical review (confirmed) — calendar invite sent.
- Aug 14: Redwood to send dedicated capacity estimate and contract addendum (we'll include a conservative buffer for cache-hosting nodes).
- Aug 18: ACME procurement sign-off target.
- Aug 24-28: Target deployment week. Redwood will provision test capacity 48 hours prior to deployment for final verification.

I attached an updated MAP PDF that includes the specific acceptance rows and suggested configuration. Please review ahead of the call if possible. On the call we'll also agree on which model variant to fall back to when memory swapping is detected.

If you want us to re-run any specific subset (e.g., 256k streaming with different chunk overlaps), flag it today and we'll include it in the final verification.

Thanks,
